summary.intent: Establish a succinct, reader-scoped writing standard (doc comments, commits, PRs, specs) across the agent-plugins ecosystem, then reduce token usage across agents and ship the result with proper semver and changelogs.
summary.outcome: Added a Reader-Scoped Writing standard wired into implementer, reviewer, drafter and auditor, unwrapped hard-wrapped markdown across the repo, trimmed descriptions, split hazard references, and added a byte-identical <constitution> section to all 38 agents (ADR-006). Fixed basis scaffolder/auditor, bumped versions across all 9 plugins with changelogs, and committed as 3074819 (v3.3.0); the behavioral smoke test is deferred.

repo: shared/constitution.md is authoring-time only and runtime agents do not load it, so rules only take effect when baked into agent prompts (goal/judgment/output) and enforced by a fresh-context reviewer or auditor.
Reference files work for short single-purpose agents via <load_first>; for multi-step loops like implementer, baking the rule into the prompt body is more reliable.
docs-voice.md covers prose artifacts (commits, PRs, changesets, docs); code-comments.md was added for doc/inline comments.
plugins/*/subagents and plugins/*/shared are symlinks to agents/ and root shared/, so 335 glob matches are only 117 real .md files; dedupe by realpath before sweeping.
Agent files now use a 5-part structure with <constitution> first, then backstory/goal/judgment/output. The constitution block must be copied byte-for-byte, since paraphrasing breaks cache sharing.
basis:scaffolder and basis:auditor encode the agent structure; any structural change must update them or the auditor will fail every conformant agent.

Version consistency requires plugin.json, README Version line, per-plugin CHANGELOG top entry and the marketplace.json entry to agree (scripts/check-versions.sh). The marketplace aggregate version bumps to the max semver level of the release.
ADRs and CHANGELOGs are historical records: add a new ADR plus a superseded/extended-by note instead of rewriting.
Agent and skill description frontmatter loads into every session as a fixed tax, so it is the highest-leverage token target; guideline is 80-200 words.
Reference files have a ~120-line cap, now enforced by the new scripts/check-reference-size.sh.
Markdown must not be hard-wrapped (the user has a standing feedback memory); YAML >-folded descriptions were also wrapped in 28 of 34 agent files.
`claude plugin validate --strict <dir>` is a useful structural check that all 9 plugins pass.

The proof skill invoked in-session loads from the marketplace cache (~/.claude/plugins/cache/orin-dx-agent-plugins/...), not the local checkout, so local edits cannot be behaviorally tested until pushed and the plugin updated.
workflow: Measure with real diffs and word counts before claiming savings, and report where the change adds cost as well as where it saves.
Read an agent's actual task before changing its model tier; graph/intake looked like a haiku candidate but needs real intent inference.
Propose before changing when the user asks, and escalate architectural rule changes (e.g. the 4-part structure) instead of amending them unilaterally.
Script byte-identical edits across many files and verify with a set-of-distinct-blocks check rather than editing by hand.
Heuristic wrap detectors give many false positives (label pairs, conditional branches); verify by hand before bulk edits.
Structural checks (YAML, versions, mermaid) do not substitute for behavioral testing of new conditional prompt logic.
Pushing to a remote needs explicit user approval, separate from a request to run a smoke test.

friction: Repeatedly hard-wrapped markdown despite the user's standing rule, which prompted an angry correction and a repo-wide cleanup.
The initial doc-comment sweep offer was based on a toposort_impl example that was from another repo (callisto).
The wrap-detection heuristic produced noisy false positives, requiring several passes and manual review.
The plugin cache mismatch blocked a live behavioral test of the local edits.
The constitution rollout initially left basis scaffolder/auditor stale, which would have failed every conformant agent; found only during the extra cleanup pass.
The <constitution> block adds ~177 words per invocation to agents with no offsetting savings.
open_items: Run the behavioral smoke test (proof against the toy target) after pushing to orin-dx/agent-plugins, running `claude plugin update`, and restarting the session; adversary's taxonomy-branching <load_first> and scanner's hazard-focus branching are unverified.
Commit 3074819 is local and has not been pushed.
Interactive Claude Code sessions outside the plugin pipeline have no reviewer/exit-gate backstop; the user accepted this.
Further description trims risk losing routing signal; adversary, architect and canon/exit-gate were left dense by choice.
